title: New Orleans man indicted for firearm and ammunition possession as a felon
text:
New Orleans man indicted for firearm and ammunition possession as a felon
A New Orleans man has been indicted for possessing a firearm and ammunition as a convicted felon. Authorities say JOHRON WILTZ faces significant penalties if found guilty following his recent arrest.
JOHRON WILTZ, age 21, was indicted on Oct. 23 for being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, according to U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.
According to the indictment, WILTZ was previously convicted of multiple felonies in Orleans Parish on April 1, including illegal possession of stolen things valued over $25,000. Less than two months later, on May 28, WILTZ was arrested while in possession of a Glock Model 19 firearm and additional ammunition.
If convicted on both offenses, WILTZ faces up to 15 years in prison, up to a $250,000 fine, and up to three years of supervised release for each count. Each count also carries a mandatory $100 special assessment fee.
Courcelle said that the indictment is merely an allegation, and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.
The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and Louisiana Probation and Parole investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney David Berman from the Violent Crime Unit is leading the prosecution.
Project Safe Neighborhoods is described as the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative aimed at coordinating efforts among law enforcement agencies at all levels to combat violent crime. The program operates within each federal district under U.S. Attorneys’ offices with strategies tailored to local needs.
